headline: South Asia: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce.
- Africa: Ukraine: firefighters battle flames and rescue dog from Kyiv ruins.
- Asia: US, Japan rehearse coordinated strikes to challenge PLA control of waters near Taiwan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Air Force awards Lockheed Martin $694M hypersonic missile production contract.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: US Air Force awards Lockheed Martin $694M hypersonic missile production contract.
The Air Force granted Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract in late September for the production and fielding of the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, or ARRW.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Pentagon creates advisory council on human performance, health.
After creating a new directorate on warfighter optimization within the Department of Defense, the Pentagon announced it will form a federal advisory committee to weigh in on issues affecting troop performance and health.
- Military Times, 5 hours ago: Navy identifies NAS Pensacola sailors killed in car crash.
The U.S. Navy shared the names of the service members who died in a Florida car crash early Saturday morning.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: Harry Kane beats Messi to 2026 Ballon d’Or.

- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: Pope Leo XIV confirms trip to Argentina following lung surgery.
‘I look forward to returning to the continent,’ the pontiff said. He will also visit Uruguay and Peru La entrada Pope Leo XIV confirms trip to Argentina following lung surgery se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE

- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Zelenskyy: Russia has launched over 100 ballistic missiles against Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast in past two weeks.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russians attack firefighters while they tackle blaze in Kramatorsk – photos, video.
Firefighters have come under a Russian double-tap strike while tackling a fire caused by Russian strikes in Kramatorsk, Donetsk Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Finnish foreign minister: We do not seek to mediate in the war because we stand with Ukraine.
Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen says Finland will continue to support Ukraine and the US-led peace process, accusing Russia of escalating the war and killing civilians.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russian attack damages school stadium in Dnipro.
The grounds of a school were damaged as a result of a Russian attack on Dnipro on 27 October. Early reports indicate that no students or staff were injured.

- Balkan Insight, 16 hours ago: Bosnian Court Verdicts for Wartime Sexual Violence Show Leniency and Disparities.

- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: EIB to sign framework deal with Canada on critical raw materials.
Deal marks concrete step toward closer ties between the EU and Canada.
- Balkan Insight, 17 hours ago: Journalist-Turned-PM Faces Daunting Challenges in Romania.
Luca Niculescu, Romania’s recently-chosen prime minister, is an experienced administrator and skilled negotiator, but has limited time and political support to tackle pressing economic and social challenges.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after Oct 2025 truce.
Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October’s US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday. The report ​by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, examined violations ‌against Palestinian civilians, including children, since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas on October 7, 2023, up to September this year.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, Africanews, 14 hours ago: Sudan drone strikes kill 21, cause mass outages in east.
Sudan’s warring sides have traded drone strikes that killed 21 people in the western Darfur region and left vast swathes of the country’s east without electricity, medics and witnesses said Tuesday. A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the de facto capital of Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Darfur, killed 21 people and wounded at least 40 others, a medical source and witnesses told AFP. One Nyala resident said a market in the city’s north was struck by a drone on Monday around 8pm (11pm PKT). Another said the market was frequented by young men, particularly RSF fighters.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 17 hours ago: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack.
The Jordanian military said it had struck “terrorist organisations” in neighbouring Syria on Monday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings. It said air force jets had “destroyed several terrorist positions” and killed and wounded “numerous members” of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack. Syrian authorities reported civilian casualties from the raids, with health officials in Daraa province saying six people, including three children and a woman, were killed.

This growth highlights not only India's manufacturing strengths but also its expanding international partnerships. European countries are eager to restock their military supplies, which bodes well for the future of India's defence industry.
